fig1_buckingham_collapse.svg: Buckingham $\Pi$ theorem in action. buckingham_pi returns the lone null vector of the pendulum's dimension matrix, $(T,L,g,m)=(2,-1,1,0)$, so the only dimensionless group is $\Pi=gT^2/L$. Top: the small-angle period $T=2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$ gives wildly different curves on the Moon, Earth and Jupiter. Bottom: forming $\Pi$ collapses all three onto the single constant $4\pi^2$ — the period law $T\propto\sqrt{L/g}$ with no equation of motion solved.
fig2_optimal_truncation.svg: The divergent asymptotic series $g(x)=xe^xE_1(x)\sim\sum_k(-1)^k k!/x^k$ evaluated by optimal_truncation. For each $x$ the error $|S_N-g|$ falls to a minimum near $N\approx x$ (dots, dotted lines) — of order the smallest term $\sim\sqrt{2\pi x}\,e^{-x}$ — then blows up as the $k!$ terms overwhelm $x^{-k}$. Adding more terms makes it worse: the hallmark of an asymptotic (non-convergent) series, and exactly how WKB and high-order perturbation theory behave.
